headline_marked: Govt to create [[accurate lists of Freedom Fighters]], martyrs and Birangonas
headline: Govt to create accurate lists of Freedom Fighters, martyrs and Birangonas
summary: The Ministry of Liberation War Affairs is coordinating with researchers and historians to remove irregularities and ensure a reliable national database.
details: The government has launched an initiative to create accurate and verified lists of martyrs, Freedom Fighters, and Birangonas of the Liberation War. The Ministry of Liberation War Affairs held a consultation meeting on Wednesday to determine the strategies for this process.

Liberation War Minister Ahmed Azam Khan stated that there have been long-standing allegations of irregularities and the inclusion of non-freedom fighters in the lists. He emphasized that it is the state's moral and historical duty to ensure the history is presented accurately to future generations.

The new lists will be developed by coordinating documentary evidence, government and military records, wartime records, eyewitness testimonies, and research-based data. The ministry aims to move away from reliance on emotion or guesswork.

The process will involve field-level data collection across villages, unions, upazilas, and districts. This will include the involvement of local freedom fighters, their families, eyewitnesses, administration, researchers, and students to build a reliable national database.

The initiative also focuses on creating a comprehensive list of martyrs, including not only those killed on the battlefield but also civilians, teachers, students, intellectuals, and women killed by the Pakistani occupation forces and their collaborators.

The ministry will ensure that the distinct state recognition and dignity of armed freedom fighters are maintained while documenting the broader national participation in the war. All evidence and sources for each name will be preserved for future research.
caption:

He emphasized that it is the state's moral and historical duty to ensure the history is presented accurately to future generations.

The new lists will be developed by coordinating documentary evidence, government and military records, wartime records, eyewitness testimonies, and research-based data. The ministry aims to move away from reliance on emotion or guesswork.

The process will involve field-level data collection across villages, unions, upazilas, and districts. This will include the involvement of local freedom fighters, their families, eyewitnesses, administration, researchers, and students to build a reliable national database.

The initiative also focuses on creating a comprehensive list of martyrs, including not only those killed on the battlefield but also civilians, teachers, students, intellectuals, and women killed by the Pakistani occupation forces and their collaborators.

The ministry will ensure that the distinct state recognition and dignity of armed freedom fighters are maintained while documenting the broader national participation in the war. All evidence and sources for each name will be preserved for future research.

headline_marked: Energy saving: [[Shops, malls directed to close by 8pm]] nationwide
headline: Energy saving: Shops, malls directed to close by 8pm nationwide
summary: The government has ordered all shopping malls and markets to shut by 8pm and turn off illuminated billboards by 7pm to save electricity.
details: The government has directed all shopping malls, markets, and shops across the country to close by 8pm as part of electricity saving and management efforts.
A memo issued by the Coordination-2 branch of the electricity department on Wednesday night specified that these establishments can now remain open from 11am to 8pm.
Additionally, all illuminated billboards must be turned off by 7pm, and all decorative lighting must be completely shut down.
The new directive also applies to fairs, trade fairs, and cultural programs, which must now conclude by 8pm.
However, certain essential services, including food shops, hospitals, and pharmacies, are exempt from these restrictions.
This is a change from the previous directive issued on June 11, which allowed shopping malls and markets to remain open until 9pm, effectively reducing the operating hours by one hour.
